```{r, warning=F, message=F,   results='hide'}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidylog)
library(lubridate)

crashes <- read.csv("data/crashes.csv")

crashes %>% count(INJURIES_FATAL)
crashes %>% count(INJURIES_INCAPACITATING)

# are the NA rows the same? Yes -- keep as NA for now
  crashes_serious_na <- crashes %>% filter(is.na(INJURIES_FATAL))

# Count serious injuries
  crashes$INJURIES_SERIOUS <- crashes$INJURIES_FATAL + crashes$INJURIES_INCAPACITATING

# Aggregate over COMPLETE weeks
  crashes$CRASH_DATE <- as.Date(crashes$CRASH_DATE)
  
  first_day <- min(crashes$CRASH_DATE, na.rm = TRUE)
  last_day  <- max(crashes$CRASH_DATE, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  first_week <- ceiling_date(first_day, "week", week_start = 7,
                             change_on_boundary = FALSE)               # first Sunday on/after first_day
  last_week  <- floor_date(last_day + 1, "week", week_start = 7) - 7   # last Sunday whose Saturday is <= last_day
  
  weekly <- crashes %>%
    mutate(WEEK_START = floor_date(CRASH_DATE, "week", week_start = 7)) %>%
    filter(WEEK_START >= first_week, WEEK_START <= last_week) %>%
    group_by(WEEK_START) %>%
    summarise(INJURIES_SERIOUS_WEEKLY = sum(INJURIES_SERIOUS, na.rm = TRUE), # NAs treated as zero, in effect
              .groups = "drop")

```

## Reproduce Current Results 


#### Helper functions

<br>
The log-likelihood of the Poisson distribution:
$$
\ell(\lambda) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left[ x_i \log \lambda - \lambda - \log(x_i!) \right]
$$

```{r}
# computationally safe form
poisson.ll <- function(lambda, x) {
  sum(x) * log(lambda) - length(x) * lambda - sum(lfactorial(x))
}
```

<br>

Derivative of the log-likelihood of the Poisson distribution:
$$
\frac{d\ell}{d\lambda} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i}{\lambda} - n
$$

```{r}
poisson.dll <- function(lambda, x) {
  sum(x) / lambda - length(x)
}
```


<br>

Second Derivative of the log-likelihood of the Poisson distribution:

$$
\frac{d^2\ell}{d\lambda^2} = -\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i}{\lambda^2}
$$

```{r}
poisson.ddll <- function(lambda, x) {
  - sum(x) / lambda^2
}
```

<br>

#### Estimating Poisson Intensity with Newton-Raphson

<br>

Function to implement Newton-Raphson algorithm: 
```{r}
# modifications: 
  # x reassignment changed from plus to minus
  # while loop tolerance: "<" changed to ">"
  # function takes data, which is automatically fed into the first and second derivative functions of the poisson log-liklihood
  # No secant approximations of second derivative

poisson.nr <- function(lambda_0, x, tol=1e-6, max.iter=20){
  
  lambda <- lambda_0
  i <- 0
  results <- data.frame(iter=i,lambda=lambda, poisson.dll=poisson.dll(lambda, x)) # starting point
  
  while (abs(poisson.dll(lambda, x))>tol && i<max.iter) {
    i <- i + 1
    lambda <- lambda - poisson.dll(lambda, x) / poisson.ddll(lambda, x)
    results <- rbind(results,data.frame(iter=i,lambda=lambda, poisson.dll=poisson.dll(lambda, x)))}
  return(results)}
```

<br>

Run the algorithm: 
```{r}
poisson.nr(50, weekly$INJURIES_SERIOUS_WEEKLY)
```

```{r}
mean(weekly$INJURIES_SERIOUS_WEEKLY) # sanity check
```

<br>

#### Replicate Results with Gradient Descent algorithm

```{r}
poisson.gd <- function(lambda_0, x, b=0.5, tol=1e-6, max.iter=40){
  i <- 0
  lambda <- lambda_0
  results <- data.frame(iter=i, lambda=lambda, poisson.ll=poisson.ll(lambda, x)) # starting point

  while (abs(poisson.dll(lambda, x))>tol & i<max.iter) {
    i <- i + 1
    t <- 1
    
    while ((poisson.ll(lambda + t*poisson.dll(lambda, x), x)) < poisson.ll(lambda, x) & t>tol) {
      t <- t*b
    }
    
    lambda <- lambda + t*poisson.dll(lambda, x)                                           
    results <- rbind(results,data.frame(iter=i,lambda=lambda, poisson.ll=poisson.ll(lambda, x)))
  }
  
  return(results)
}

poisson.gd(50, weekly$INJURIES_SERIOUS_WEEKLY) %>% tail(5)
```

## Modeling Crash Data with Negative Binomial Distribution

<br>

##### Find Parameters with Gradient Descent

<br>

Gradient descent struggles to find MLEs for $(r, p)$ parametrization. Instead, we use Claude Sonnet 5.5 to model this with $(r, μ)$ paramaterization, then back so we can compare with Q2. 

<br>

<details>
  <summary>Show/Hide Equations</summary>

In this parametrization the pmf is
$$P(X = k) = \frac{\Gamma(k + r)}{\Gamma(r)\,k!}\left(\frac{r}{r+\mu}\right)^{r}\left(\frac{\mu}{r+\mu}\right)^{k},$$
and the log-likelihood for counts $x_1, \dots, x_n$ is
$$\ell(r, \mu) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \log\Gamma(x_i + r) - n\log\Gamma(r) - \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log(x_i!) + n r \log\frac{r}{r+\mu} + \left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i\right)\log\frac{\mu}{r+\mu}.$$
<br>

Differentiating gives
$$\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial r} = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\psi(x_i + r) - n\,\psi(r) + n\left[\log\frac{r}{r+\mu} + 1\right] - \frac{n r + \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i}{r + \mu},$$
$$\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i}{\mu} - \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i + n r}{r + \mu},$$
where $\psi$ is the digamma function. Setting $\partial \ell / \partial \mu = 0$ gives $\hat{\mu} = \bar{x}$ for any $r$, so $\mu$ is decoupled from $r$, which is why this parametrization is well conditioned.

Because we optimize over $\theta = (\log r, \log \mu)$, the chain rule gives
$$\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \log r} = r\,\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial r}, \qquad \frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \log \mu} = \mu\,\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \mu}.$$
In the code, $\ell$ and its gradient are divided by $n$ (the per-observation scale) so the course's step-size rule behaves.

After convergence, we recover the original parameters:
$$\hat{r} = e^{\hat\theta_1}, \qquad \hat{\mu} = e^{\hat\theta_2}, \qquad \hat{p} = \frac{\hat r}{\hat r + \hat \mu}.$$
</details>

<br>

```{r}
x_data <- weekly$INJURIES_SERIOUS_WEEKLY
n  <- length(x_data)
sx <- sum(x_data)

# Log-likelihood per observation. theta = c(log r, log mu)
  nb.ll.mu <- function(theta) {
    r <- exp(theta[1]); mu <- exp(theta[2])
    (sum(lgamma(x_data + r)) - n * lgamma(r) - sum(lfactorial(x_data)) +
       n * r * log(r / (r + mu)) + sx * log(mu / (r + mu))) / n
  }

# Gradient with respect to theta = c(log r, log mu), per observation
  nb.grad.mu <- function(theta) {
    r <- exp(theta[1]); mu <- exp(theta[2])
    d_r  <- sum(digamma(x_data + r)) - n * digamma(r) +
              n * (log(r / (r + mu)) + 1) - (n * r + sx) / (r + mu)
    d_mu <- sx / mu - (sx + n * r) / (r + mu)
    c(r * d_r, mu * d_mu) / n          # chain rule for the logs, then per observation
  }

# Gradient descent with backtracking line search
  graddesc <- function(f, g, x0, b=0.8, tol=1e-2, max.iter=40){
    i <- 0
    x <- x0
    results <- t(c(0,x,-f(x)))
    while (sqrt(g(x)%*%g(x))>tol & i<max.iter) {
      i <- i + 1
      t <- 1
      while ((f(x+t*g(x))<f(x)) & t>tol) {
        t <- t*b}
      x <- x + t*g(x)
      results <- rbind(results,t(c(i,x,-f(x))))}
    colnames(results) <- c('iter',paste0('x',1:length(x)),'f')
    return(results)}

# Method-of-moments starting values
  m <- mean(x_data); v <- var(x_data)
  x0 <- c(log(m^2 / (v - m)), log(m))

# Run it
  out <- graddesc(nb.ll.mu, nb.grad.mu, x0, tol = 1e-4, max.iter = 1000)
  tail(out, 3)

# Transform back to the (r, p) parameterization
  theta_hat <- out[nrow(out), c("x1", "x2")]
  r_hat  <- exp(theta_hat[["x1"]])
  mu_hat <- exp(theta_hat[["x2"]])
  p_hat  <- r_hat / (r_hat + mu_hat)
  c(r = r_hat, p = p_hat, mu = mu_hat)
```
